# Billing System Migration Rollout Plan
**Scope:** Migrate 40,000 existing users from legacy billing system to new billing system. Both systems run in parallel throughout the migration to allow safe rollback per batch.

---

## Phase 1: Canary (2% of users — 800 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed end-to-end parity testing in staging against a replayed sample of production billing events (charges, refunds, proration, tax calculation, dunning) with 100% output match against the old system for that sample, and rollback tooling (re-pointing a user back to the old system) has been tested successfully at least once.

**Population:** Internal employee accounts and opted-in low-risk external users (no active disputes, no enterprise contracts, monthly billing only).

**Duration:** Minimum 5 business days, covering at least one full billing cycle event (invoice generation) for the cohort.

---

## Phase 2: Early Adopters (15% of users — 6,000 users, cumulative 17%)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completed its full observation window with zero critical billing discrepancies (see halt metric below), support ticket volume for migrated users within 1.5x of baseline, and finance has reconciled Phase 1 invoiced amounts against expected amounts with no unresolved variance.

**Population:** Randomly sampled self-serve monthly and annual subscribers, excluding customers on custom contracts, active payment disputes, or in a grace/dunning state.

**Duration:** Minimum 10 business days, covering at least one annual-billing edge case cohort if available.

---

## Phase 3: General Availability (63% of users — 25,200 users, cumulative 80%)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 completed with error rate below the halt threshold, at least one full monthly *and* one full annual billing cycle observed end-to-end with correct invoicing, tax, and dunning behavior, and customer support has confirmed runbooks/training are ready for full-volume ticket load.

**Population:** All remaining standard accounts (self-serve, SMB, monthly and annual), migrated in waves of ~10% every 3–5 business days to preserve the ability to halt mid-phase.

**Duration:** Minimum 3 weeks.

---

## Phase 4: Final Batch — High-Complexity Accounts (20% of users — 8,000 users, cumulative 100%)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 3 fully complete with cumulative discrepancy rate below threshold for 3 consecutive weeks, enterprise/legal sign-off obtained for contract-billing edge cases (multi-entity invoicing, custom tax arrangements, negotiated payment terms), and a dedicated white-glove support rotation is staffed for this cohort.

**Population:** Enterprise accounts, custom-contract customers, accounts with active disputes or non-standard payment terms — migrated in small batches (~5% at a time) with manual verification of the first invoice cycle per batch.

**Note:** The old billing system remains fully operational, unmodified, and untouched by any decommissioning activity during this phase. Old-system decommissioning is explicitly out of scope for Phase 4 and is deferred to a separate post-migration Phase 5 (sunset), which begins only after Phase 4's final batch has completed at least one full billing cycle with clean reconciliation.

---

## Halt Metrics

Automated rollout progression pauses immediately (no further users migrated to the next batch/phase) if, within any 24-hour window:

- **Billing discrepancy rate exceeds 0.5%** of migrated users' invoices (amount mismatch, duplicate charge, or missed charge vs. expected), OR
- **Payment failure rate for migrated users exceeds 2x** the trailing 30-day baseline failure rate for the old system, OR
- **Support tickets tagged "billing-migration"** exceed 3% of the currently-migrated user population in a single day.

Any halt triggers an incident review before migration resumes; a rollback of the affected batch to the old system must be available within 4 hours of a halt decision.

---

## Risks

RISK: Duplicate or missed charges during dual-system cutover for a given user | Implement idempotent charge keys and a reconciliation job comparing both systems' ledgers daily during migration | Billing Platform Eng Lead
RISK: Tax calculation differences between old and new systems causing under/over-collection | Run parallel shadow tax calculations for all migrated users for first two billing cycles and alert on any variance above $0.01 | Finance/Tax Compliance Owner
RISK: Enterprise customers with custom contract terms are migrated incorrectly, damaging key accounts | Exclude all custom-contract accounts from automated phases; require manual account-team sign-off before each Phase 4 batch | Enterprise Account Management Lead
RISK: Support team overwhelmed by migration-related tickets during GA phase | Pre-train support staff on new system, stagger Phase 3 waves at 10% increments, and staff a temporary migration support queue | Customer Support Manager
RISK: Rollback path fails when needed, stranding users mid-migration | Test rollback procedure in Phase 1 and re-validate it before entering Phase 3 (highest volume phase) | SRE/Infrastructure Lead

PHASES: 4
